cards.claim: Early layers in DNNs converge faster than later layers during training
cards.conditions: General DNN training (early layers responsible for low-level feature extraction, fewer parameters)
cards.effect: Early layers can be frozen earlier without accuracy loss
cards.quote: For example, the early layers in DNNs are responsible for low-level features extraction and usually have fewer parameters than the later layers, making the early layers converge faster during training.

cards.claim: Different layers require different training epochs to stabilize, and stabilization timing is non-monotonic with depth
cards.conditions: ResNet50 fine-tuning on CIFAR-10 (pre-trained on ImageNet)
cards.effect: Later layers can sometimes stabilize faster than earlier layers due to residual connections; adaptive per-layer timing is necessary rather than sequential freezing
cards.evidence: Empirical observation from representational similarity (CKA) curves in Figure 4
cards.quote: Moreover, different layers require different training epochs to stabilize, and basically the layers in the front stabilize faster than the layers in the back (e.g., layers 10 and 20 stabilize faster than layers 40 and 50). But it is interesting to see that the layer in the back is possible to stabilize faster than the front layer (e.g., layer 30 stabilizes faster than layers 10 and 20). This is due to the presence of residual connections in the ResNet architecture, which allows some of the later layers to behave like the earlier layers.

cards.claim: Layer representational similarity (CKA) stabilization is a valid signal for freezing readiness
cards.conditions: Comparing layer outputs to well-trained reference model using Centered Kernel Alignment (CKA)
cards.effect: When CKA stabilizes, layer features change minimally with continued training; freezing has little accuracy impact
cards.evidence: Methodological design and Figure 4 observation in Section 3.4
cards.quote: Further, if the CKA value of a layer stabilizes during the training process, we consider this layer is converged and ready to be frozen. CKA is obtained by comparing the output feature maps of two layers under the same input image batch. A higher CKA value indicates that the two layers will output more similar feature maps with the same inputs. Further, if the CKA value of a layer stabilizes during the training process, we consider this layer is converged and ready to be frozen.

cards.claim: Layer convergence is non-monotonic (noisy); optimization trajectories fluctuate rather than smoothly converge
cards.conditions: ResNet50 fine-tuning on CIFAR-10 (pre-trained on ImageNet), observing CKA curves across epochs
cards.effect: Recent weight history does not always reflect optimal direction; long-term convergence patterns must be considered rather than greedy local signals
cards.evidence: Empirical observation from Figure 4 and explicit design rationale in Section 3.2
cards.quote: Moreover, the similarity with the well-trained model is not monotonically increasing but fluctuating, which correlates with our discussion in section 3.2 that it is not always the most recent model that has the most significant impact on the current model parameters.

cards.claim: Representational similarity-guided freezing (CKA-based) can save substantial computation while maintaining accuracy
cards.conditions: ResNet50 and VGG11 models pre-trained on ImageNet, then trained on CIFAR-100 for 10 epochs with per-epoch freezing decisions
cards.effect: 48% computation reduction (TFLOPs) for ResNet50; 44% for VGG11; accuracy maintained or slightly improved
cards.evidence: Table 1 experimental results comparing full training vs. similarity-guided freezing in Section 3.4
cards.quote: As shown in the table, training the networks using the representational similarity-guided freezing method can significantly reduce the computation cost (e.g., it saves 48% computation for training ResNet50) while maintaining the model accuracy, demonstrating the effectiveness of our similarity-guided labeling method and the correctness of the generated dataset.

cards.claim: BatchNorm layers can be frozen together with their corresponding Conv layers to save backward-propagation computation
cards.conditions: CNN models with BatchNorm (ResNet50, VGG11, MobileNetV2); part of SmartFRZ framework
cards.effect: Avoids unnecessary gradient computation in backward pass; enables partial layer freezing
cards.quote: In CNN models, we freeze the BN layer together with its corresponding CONV layer to avoid unnecessary computation costs in back-propagation.
